intro: Once upon a time, humanity had a perfect home.
Earth gave us air to breathe, clean water, food and a sky that kept us safe. All of it for free.
But we took more than Earth could give. Factories and fires filled the air with smoke. Droughts dried the fields. Acid rain poisoned the lakes and the soil.
The satellites warned us, and we did not listen.
When the sky turned gray, humanity built one last hope: Project Phoenix, a base on Mars.
For four nights, one commander kept it running. Water. Oxygen. Food. Energy.
Now the first colonists have landed.
good: The base was ready. Every tank was full, and every colonist had air, water and food from the very first day.
Year after year, more ships arrived. Greenhouses grew into gardens, and children were born under a red sky.
On Mars, humanity learned what Earth had always done for us. That knowledge went home, and slowly, Earth's sky began to clear.
And that is how humanity was saved: one breath, one drop, one choice at a time.
mid: The colonists made it, but the base was short of {res}. Everyone had to ration.
The first years were hard, and every day was a careful balance.
But humanity held on, and the base grew stronger along with its people.
Humanity survived, just barely. Its future depends on learning from every mistake.
bad: The colonists stepped out of the ship, but the base could not keep water, oxygen, food and energy going at once.
Tanks ran dry and the lights flickered. The colonists had to go back to their ship and wait in orbit, far from a home that was not ready.
On Earth, the sky stayed gray.
Humanity had made the same mistake twice: it did not take care of its life support in time.
Maybe next time, the story can end differently.

good.title: THE BASE IS READY
good.yana: Every choice you made keeps someone alive.

bad.title: THE BASE WAS NOT READY
bad.yana: A base needs all four at once. Try another plan?
